title: A Protocol for the Gravity
premise: Ivo Galloway, the last human technician aboard the automated relay station Meridian-9, has spent five years hauling cargo through contested orbits, keeping his head down while the colonial fleet and the corporate Combine wage a cold war of sanctions and silence. When the colony's children begin sharing an identical dream — a signal rising from dead space that no instrument can detect — Ivo discovers the dreams are a distress call from the Combine's disappeared dissidents, broadcast on a frequency only young minds can parse. Racing the expiration of the fleet's fragile truce, Ivo and two dream-touched children pilot a battered tug toward the relay at the edge of dead space to amplify the signal before the fleet's jamming grid comes online. In the end, the truth reaches every mind in the system at once; the truce collapses not into war but into reckoning, and Ivo — who survived by belonging to no one — finally chooses a people.
about_author: Mara Delacroix is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for automated freight systems before turning to fiction. She writes from a coastal town where she claims the tides taught her everything she knows about patience and plot.

chapters.title: Cargo and Quiet
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A routine haul through contested orbits establishes his solitary life aboard Meridian-9: the drones he maintains, the fleet check-ins he fakes warmth for, the five-year habit of belonging to no one. The emotional beat is comfortable loneliness — a man who has made peace with being expendable.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream Together
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Sefa, a nine-year-old dockworker's daughter on the colony ring, who wakes reciting coordinates she shouldn't know. Forty other children share the dream. Her mother dismisses it; Sefa writes the numbers on her wall. The beat is eerie wonder curdling into fear as adults refuse to listen.

chapters.title: Ghost Frequency
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Meridian-9's instruments register nothing, but the station's oldest relay coil hums at 3 a.m., resonating with something below detection threshold. Ivo logs it, deletes the log, then restores it. The beat is a technician's superstition meeting evidence he can't explain away.

chapters.title: Truce Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Fleet liaison Officer Brandt's POV. She calculates the truce's expiry against Combine fleet movements and realizes the jamming grid deployment is already scheduled — peace was always a countdown. She withholds this from Ivo, her only asset in contested space. The beat is institutional guilt.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Knocked
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Sefa stows away on a cargo pallet bound for Meridian-9, having traced the coordinates to the station herself. Ivo finds her in the airlock, furious and outmaneuvered by a child. The beat is reluctant connection — his first obligation to another person in five years.

chapters.title: What the Dead Space Says
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. She describes the dream in detail: a room of voices, a door, a name repeated — her uncle's name, one of the disappeared. Ivo cross-references and finds the vanished dissidents were last routed through dead space. The beat is grief becoming purpose.

chapters.title: Sanctions and Silence
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. The Combine blocks all traffic near dead space under sanction law; any vessel entering will be seized or destroyed after the truce expires. Brandt quietly falsifies Ivo's next clearance route — toward dead space — knowing it may be a death sentence. The beat is complicity as mercy.

chapters.title: The Tug Called Patience
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He preps the ancient tug Patience for a run no insurance will cover, teaching Sefa basic systems because leaving her behind means the fleet will study her like a specimen. The beat is fear transmuted into competence; two outsiders building trust through work.

chapters.title: Second Dreamer
chapters.summary: New character Teo, sixteen, arrives uninvited — the oldest dreamer, whose version of the dream includes the ending: the signal dying. He insists the children's connection weakens nightly. The trio now has a deadline inside the deadline. The beat is dread sharpening resolve.

chapters.title: Departure Window
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. She covers their escape with a manufactured cargo emergency, burning her career in the process, and transmits one line to Ivo: 'Before the grid.' The beat is sacrifice without absolution — she acts justly knowing the institution never will.

chapters.title: Contested Orbits
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The Patience threads debris fields and Combine picket lines; a near-miss forces Ivo to dump cargo to survive, erasing his livelihood. Sefa navigates by dream-memory when sensors fail. The beat is terror shared openly for the first time — survival as collaboration.

chapters.title: The Edge of the Map
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. Past the last beacon, dead space is genuinely silent — no traffic, no light but theirs. Teo confesses his dream shows him dying at the relay. Ivo refuses to accept it as fate. The beat is defiance against inevitability, a father-figure forming in real time.

chapters.title: Derelict
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. They find the Combine's hidden facility: a derelict station where the disappeared were held, its life support long failed, its prisoners' final messages stored in the same undetectable frequency — the source of the dream. The beat is horror and witness; justice begins with seeing.

chapters.title: Voices in the Coil
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Inside the derelict, the dream becomes waking: Sefa hears the recorded voices directly, including her uncle's last message naming the officials who ordered the disappearances. The children realize they aren't receivers — they're the archive. The beat is terrible inheritance.

chapters.title: Combine Interdiction
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV: Combine security chief Vess, dispatched to erase the derelict before the truce ends, closes on the Patience. Vess is not a monster but a believer in order — the story's argument given flesh. The beat is cold, reasonable menace.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Cornered, Ivo faces his old doctrine — survive alone — and rejects it: he broadcasts their position to draw Vess off the children, nearly dying in the exchange. The beat is the theme made action; belonging costs everything he used to be.

chapters.title: Amplify
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. At the derelict's core, the trio splices the Patience's relay coil into the prison's transmitter, betting the fleet's jamming grid can't blanket a frequency it doesn't believe exists. Teo's dream-ending looms. The beat is desperate engineering as prayer.

chapters.title: The Signal Rises
chapters.summary: Climax, rotating POVs. The transmission fires — every child in the system wakes speaking the names; Vess's own daughter among them. Vess stands down rather than fire on a signal his crew can hear. The jamming grid deploys too late, jamming nothing. The beat is truth as unstoppable physics.

chapters.title: Reckoning, Not War
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. The fleet's truce expires into scandal instead of battle: the named officials are arrested, the Combine fractures, and Brandt's falsified clearances become evidence of conscience. The beat is justice arriving outside the law that failed to provide it.

chapters.title: What Vess Carries Home
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Stripped of command, he listens to the full archive voluntarily, then testifies — not redeemed, but unwilling to let his daughter inherit his silence. The beat is accountability chosen late, still costing, still real.

chapters.title: A Protocol for the Gravity
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The title lands: gravity is what pulls you toward people, and Ivo finally stops fighting it. He ferries the surviving families of the disappeared to see the derelict memorialized, Sefa and Teo aboard as crew, not passengers. The beat is homecoming without sentimentality.

chapters.title: The Room of Voices, Open
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV, closing frame mirroring chapter two. The dream is gone; the archive is public; the children remember it as memory, not haunting. Sefa adds her own message to the record for whoever inherits the frequency next. The beat is quiet hope — witness passed forward.
